questions.title: Triage Code Lookup
questions.description:
An emergency ward indexes patients by triage code in a binary search tree; reception must check instantly whether a code is already registered. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static boolean bstSearch(TNode root, int v)

It must return true when the triage code v exists in the tree, false otherwise.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers of the BST, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the code v.

Output Format:
One line with true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= code, v <= 100000, all codes distinct
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= code, v <= 100000, all codes distinct

questions.title: Price Range Census
questions.description:
A price-comparison service stores price points in a BST; shoppers filter by a closed range and need the number of products inside it. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int rangeCount(TNode root, int lo, int hi)

It must return how many node values fall in the inclusive range [lo, hi].

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers of the BST, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: lo. Line 4: hi (lo <= hi).

Output Format:
One line with the count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, lo, hi <= 100000, all values distinct, lo <= hi
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, lo, hi <= 100000, all values distinct, lo <= hi

questions.title: Insert into the BST
questions.description:
A binary search tree keeps smaller values left and larger values right, so every insert walks a single root-to-leaf path. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static TNode bstInsert(TNode root, int v)

It must insert v into the search tree (duplicates go to the right) and return the root of the updated tree. The harness prints the inorder traversal of the result, which shows the sorted order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description of the existing BST. Line 2: n level-order integers, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the value v to insert.

Output Format:
One line with the inorder traversal of the updated tree space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, v <= 100000, all values distinct, v is not already present
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, v <= 100000, all values distinct, v is not already present

questions.title: Parent in the Heap Array
questions.description:
A binary heap is stored flat: for the node at index i (0-based), the parent lives at index (i - 1) / 2. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int heapParent(int[] heap, int i)

It must return the value stored at the parent of index i. i is at least 1, so a parent always exists.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the heap size. Line 2: n space-separated integers — the heap array. Line 3: the index i (1 <= i <= n-1).

Output Format:
One line with the parent's value.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000, 1 <= i <= n-1

questions.title: Catalog Registration
questions.description:
A parts warehouse registers every new product code into a binary search tree so later lookups stay fast. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static TNode bstInsert(TNode root, int v)

It must insert the product code v into the search tree and return the root of the updated tree. The harness prints the inorder traversal, which lists the catalog in sorted order.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description of the existing catalog tree. Line 2: n level-order integers, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the new code v.

Output Format:
One line with the sorted catalog after the insert, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= code, v <= 100000, all codes distinct, v is not already present

questions.title: Kth Smallest in the BST
questions.description:
A trading engine keeps price points in a BST and must answer rank queries: the k-th smallest price. Count the nodes of the left subtree to decide which side to descend — no need to build the sorted list. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int kthSmallest(TNode root, int k)

It must return the k-th smallest value (1-based) in the search tree. You may write additional static helper methods if you need them.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers of the BST, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th smallest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000, all values distinct, 1 <= k <= n

questions.title: Queue Drain Simulation
questions.description:
A job scheduler pushes every submitted task into a PriorityQueue and then drains the most urgent tasks first. Simulate it: push all tasks in order, then poll exactly m times, reporting each polled priority. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static ArrayList<Integer> heapPolls(int[] values, int polls)

It must push every value of values into a java.util.PriorityQueue (a min-heap), then poll it exactly polls times, collecting the polled values in order into the returned list. Use java.util.PriorityQueue.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of tasks. Line 2: n space-separated priorities (push order). Line 3: polls, the number of polls (1 <= polls <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the polled priorities space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000, 1 <= polls <= n

questions.title: Heapify the Array
questions.description:
Turning an arbitrary array into a min-heap in place uses bottom-up sifting: sweep i from n/2 - 1 down to 0 and sift every node down. siftDown(i) compares the node with its children, swaps it with its STRICTLY smallest child (the left child wins ties) and continues from the swapped position. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static void buildMinHeap(int[] a)

It must convert a into a min-heap in place using exactly this algorithm; the harness prints the resulting array. For index i the children are 2*i + 1 and 2*i + 2.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the array size. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the heapified array space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000

It must return the smallest value in the tree strictly greater than v. A suitable slot always exists in every test.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers of the BST, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the requested time v.

Output Format:
One line with the booked slot.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= value, v <= 100000, all values distinct, a strictly greater value always exists

Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

questions.title: Validate the BST
questions.description:
A corrupted feed once planted a value in the wrong subtree; the repair tool now re-validates every tree. Checking each node against only its parent is NOT enough — every value must lie inside the whole range allowed by ALL ancestors. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static boolean isBst(TNode root, long lo, long hi)

It must return true when every value in the tree lies strictly between lo and hi (exclusive bounds) and both subtrees are valid with tightened ranges; false otherwise. The harness calls isBst(root, Long.MIN_VALUE, Long.MAX_VALUE).

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers, -1 marks a missing child.

Output Format:
One line with true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000, all values distinct

questions.title: Kth Largest Element
questions.description:
A leaderboard feed is too large to sort; keep a min-heap holding only the k largest values seen so far — its root is then exactly the k-th largest. Push each value; when the heap already holds k values and the new one beats the root, replace the root. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static int kthLargest(int[] arr, int k)

It must return the k-th largest value (1-based) of arr using a java.util.PriorityQueue as a size-k min-heap. Do not sort the array.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers. Line 3: k (1 <= k <= n).

Output Format:
One line with the k-th largest value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000, 1 <= k <= n

questions.title: Remove from the BST
questions.description:
A product is discontinued: unlink its code from the catalog BST. Deletion has three shapes — leaf (just unlink), one child (splice the child up), two children (copy the inorder successor's value into the node, then delete the successor from the right subtree). The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static TNode bstDelete(TNode root, int v)

It must remove the node holding v (v is always present) and return the root of the updated tree. The harness prints the inorder traversal of the result, still ascending. The tree keeps at least one node after the deletion.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of slots in the level-order description. Line 2: n level-order integers of the BST, -1 marks a missing child. Line 3: the value v to remove.

Output Format:
One line with the inorder traversal of the updated tree space-separated.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, v <= 100000, all values distinct, v is present, at least one node remains
questions.inputconstrains: 2 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value, v <= 100000, all values distinct, v is present, at least one node remains

questions.title: Drain in Ascending Order
questions.description:
A print queue must emit jobs from highest priority (smallest number) to lowest: push everything into a java.util.PriorityQueue (min-heap), then poll until it is empty — the drained order is ascending. The class Main and its main method are already provided. Write only the required static method:

    static ArrayList<Integer> heapSort(int[] values)

It must push every value into a java.util.PriorityQueue and return, in poll order, all of them. Do not sort with Arrays or Collections.

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
One line with the drained values space-separated (ascending).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, -100000 <= value <= 100000
